descriptionChirho: Hifil stem: to drive away, banish, or expel persons from their land or community — Arabic طَرَدَ (to expel), Korean 쫓아내다 (to drive out), Swahili -fukuza (to chase away), confirming a core exile/banishment sense distinct from leading astray.

Hifil stem: to lead astray morally or spiritually, to seduce or entice away from the right path — Arabic أَضَلَّ (to lead astray) and أَغْوَى (to seduce), Korean 빗나게 하다 (to make go astray) and 유혹하다 (to seduce), Swahili -poteza (to cause to be lost), clearly distinct from physical banishment.

Hifil stem: to thrust down or push with physical force — Arabic يَدْفَعُ (to push), Korean 떨어뜨리다 (to cause to fall), Swahili kumshusha (to bring down), indicating violent physical displacement rather than exile or enticement.

Nifal stem: to be banished or exiled, often as substantival participle 'outcast/banished one' — Arabic مَنْفِيّ / مَطْرُود (exiled, driven out), Korean 쫓겨난 자 (the one driven out), Swahili aliyefukuzwa (one who was expelled), functioning as the passive of the core Hifil banishment sense.

Nifal stem: to be drawn away or enticed internally, to be seduced from the right path — Arabic تَنْجَرِفُ (to be swept away), Korean 유혹되다 (to be seduced) and 끌리다 (to be drawn), Swahili -shawishika (to be persuaded), representing the passive of the 'lead astray' Hifil sense rather than physical exile.

Nifal stem: to be straying or wandering, describing a state of being lost — Arabic ضَالّ (straying, lost), Korean 헤매다 (to wander), Swahili -potea (to be lost), emphasizing the resulting state of aimless wandering rather than the act of expulsion.

Nifal stem: to be pushed or to slip physically — Arabic تَنْدَفِعُ (to be pushed), Korean 미끄러지다 (to slip), Swahili -telezeka (to slip), a rare physical sense of losing footing or being made to slide, distinct from exile or enticement.

Hofal and Pual passive stems: to be driven or hunted as an intensive passive — Arabic مُطَارَد (hunted, pursued) and مَطرُود (driven out), Korean 쫓겨난 (driven away), Swahili anayefukuzwa (one being chased), an emphatic passive form stressing the intensity of the banishment.

Qal stem: to swing or brandish a weapon — Arabic لِتَرْفَعَ (to lift up), Korean 들어올리다 (to lift up), Swahili kupigisha (to cause to strike), a rare physical sense of wielding or swinging an implement, entirely distinct from the banishment semantic field.
